content.text:
I made a few small styling additions to `0.html`. The file was already in good shape, so I found no bugs to fix. I haven't opened it in a browser, and since the page only contains an `<h1>`, none of the changes are visible until you add content.

## What changed

| Element | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `hr` | Flat 1px line in the text colour instead of the browser's default inset grey rule | Matches how `blockquote` and the focus outline already use the text colour |
| `a` | `text-underline-offset: 0.15em` | Keeps underlines from running through descenders |
| `dt` | Bold | Terms were indistinguishable from surrounding text |
| `th`, `td` | 1px bottom border | Rows had no separators, so tables were hard to scan |
| `caption` | Start-aligned, padded to match the cells | Default is centred, which clashed with start-aligned cells |
| `summary` | `cursor: pointer` | Signals it is clickable |

These are all judgment calls about taste, so drop any you don't like.

## What I left alone

- **Title and heading:** both are still the placeholder `0`, and there is no `<meta name="description">`. These need your real content.
- **Wide tables:** `display: block` on `table` gives horizontal scrolling without a wrapper element, but some older Safari versions drop table semantics for screen readers when it's set. If the page will carry real data tables, wrapping them in a scrollable `<div>` is safer.
